title: Lunar AeroLabs Advances LAGF800 Flight Planning, Aircraft Systems and Ground Operations in Latest Alpha Update
summary: Lunar AeroLabs reveals major progress on the LAGF800 for MSFS 2024, including expanded flight planning, improved aircraft handling, functional ground vehicles and a Ground Power Unit.
body:
# Lunar AeroLabs Advances LAGF800 Flight Planning, Aircraft Systems and Ground Operations in Latest Alpha Update

**2 November 2026 | NEWS | Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024**

Lunar AeroLabs has revealed another substantial development update for its upcoming LAGF800 ultra-long-range business jet for Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, highlighting significant progress in flight planning, avionics, aircraft handling and ground operations.

Published on 1 November 2026, the developer's latest Sunday update details improvements to the aircraft's Touch Screen Controller (TSC), flight management capabilities and handling characteristics, alongside newly implemented ground vehicles and a functional Ground Power Unit (GPU).

The announcement also confirms that alpha testing continues, with further refinements underway across several aircraft systems.

## Expanded Touch Screen Controller and Flight Planning

![](</assets/2026-11-2 Image 1.png>)

One of the most significant areas of development concerns the LAGF800's Touch Screen Controller and associated flight management functionality.

According to Lunar AeroLabs, the TSC continues to gain additional capabilities, including:

- Flight-plan modification review, execution and cancellation.
- Secondary flight plans.
- Saving and loading flight plans.
- Direct-To navigation.
- Airways, holding patterns and crossing restrictions.
- Expanded LNAV, VNAV, fuel management and aircraft information pages.
- Adjustable departure, approach and go-around speed schedules.

These additions represent an important step towards delivering the sophisticated flight management experience expected from a modern ultra-long-range business jet.

The ability to manage complex flight plans, make in-flight modifications and adjust speed schedules should be particularly relevant to pilots undertaking long-distance operations.

However, the developer has identified flight-plan management as an area still undergoing alpha testing and refinement.

## Improvements to Flight Handling and Aircraft Systems

Lunar AeroLabs has also reported several improvements to the LAGF800's flight dynamics and aircraft systems.

These include refined roll and pitch response, improved spoiler behaviour and adjustments to climb and cruise scheduling.

Engine-out logic has been improved, while in-flight engine relight capability has now been added.

Further work has focused on throttle calibration and reverse thrust operation, both important aspects of aircraft handling during ground operations and landing.

The developer continues to evaluate flight handling and flare characteristics, spoiler deployment, go-around behaviour and speed scheduling during alpha testing.

## Enhanced Passenger Cabin and Sound Environment

Development work is also progressing throughout the aircraft's passenger accommodation.

Lunar AeroLabs reports refinements to the cabin, galley, stairs and baggage areas, together with improvements to interior lighting.

The sound environment has received additional attention, with newly recorded audio integrated into the aircraft.

New sounds have also been introduced for cabinets, drawers, appliances and water systems, while battery-fan noise has been reduced.

These changes are intended to improve immersion and help create a more convincing executive aviation experience.

## Functional Ground Vehicles and Ground Power Unit

![](</assets/2026-11-2 Image 2.png>)

Another notable milestone is the implementation of the LAGF800's first set of ground vehicles.

According to Lunar AeroLabs, these vehicles are now functional within the aircraft environment, providing additional activity around the aircraft during ground operations.

The developer has also completed and integrated a Ground Power Unit (GPU).

These additions form part of Lunar AeroLabs' wider ambition to deliver a complete business aviation experience, extending beyond the cockpit to include aircraft servicing and ramp operations.

The developer's accompanying screenshots show the LAGF800 positioned on an illuminated ramp alongside ground vehicles, as well as further cockpit and aircraft-system previews.

![](</assets/2026-11-2 Image 3.png>)

## Alpha Testing Continues

Despite the progress reported in the latest update, the LAGF800 remains in alpha development.

Lunar AeroLabs has identified several ongoing testing priorities:

- Flight handling and flare characteristics.
- Spoiler deployment and go-around procedures.
- Speed scheduling and throttle calibration.
- Flight-plan management.
- Head-Up Display (HUD) and Enhanced Vision System (EVS) functionality.
- Virtual reality usability.
- Cabin interactions and night lighting.

These areas remain subject to further testing and refinement before the aircraft can progress towards release.

The developer has not announced a revised release date in this update. Its previously stated target of the third quarter of 2027 therefore remains the latest timetable communicated to the community, rather than a guaranteed launch date.

## Continuing Progress Following Navigraph Partnership

The latest development update follows Lunar AeroLabs' announcement on 29 October that it had become an official Navigraph partner.

That announcement also introduced an official LAGF800 SimBrief aircraft profile, allowing enthusiasts to begin planning flights using dedicated aircraft performance and fuel-planning information.

Together, these developments demonstrate continuing work on both the aircraft's onboard systems and its wider flight-planning environment.

## BizJet Pilot's View

The latest LAGF800 update provides encouraging evidence of progress across several important areas of the project.

The expanded Touch Screen Controller functionality and flight-management capabilities are particularly interesting, while improvements to aircraft handling and engine systems suggest that development is moving well beyond visual modelling.

The introduction of functional ground vehicles and a Ground Power Unit is another welcome addition, particularly for enthusiasts interested in recreating realistic executive aviation operations.

There is still considerable work ahead, and the aircraft remains in alpha testing. Nevertheless, the range of systems being developed makes the LAGF800 an increasingly interesting project to follow.

BizJet Pilot will continue monitoring Lunar AeroLabs' development announcements as the aircraft progresses towards its planned release.

---

**Source:** Lunar AeroLabs official Discord server, `#announcements`, Sunday development update by Golf, 1 November 2026.

**Related:** Lunar AeroLabs' Navigraph partnership and official LAGF800 SimBrief profile announcement, 29 October 2026.

*All development milestones and functionality described in this article are based on information provided by Lunar AeroLabs. Features remain subject to change during development.*
